/kamˈbja.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to exchange
  2. (transitive) to change
  3. (intransitive) to change [auxiliary essere]

Inherited from Vulgar Latin or Late Latin cambiāre, from change in conjugation of cambīre. Doublet of cangiare. Cognate with Neapolitan cagnà.

/sos.teˈne.re/

Verb

  1. to support, to hold up, to prop, to carry the weight of
    1. Synonym: reggere
  2. to sustain, to bear, to stand, to suffer
    1. Synonyms: subire, sopportare
  3. to support, to back, to stand up for, to uphold, to defend, to cheer up
    1. Synonym: appoggiare
  4. to state, to assert, to claim, to maintain
    1. Synonyms: affermare, proclamare
  5. (theater) to play, to act
  6. (philosophy) to be the arche of

From Latin sustinēre.

/ri.ɡwarˈda.re/

Verb

  1. to concern, regard, be about, deal with, speak to
    1. Synonym: concernere
  2. to take care of, look after
  3. to examine, check, go over
    1. Synonym: esaminare
  4. to look at again, have another look at

From ri- +‎ guardare. Compare French regarder.

/ˈlɛd.d͡ʒe.re/

Verb

  1. (ambitransitive) to read [auxiliary avere]

Adjective

  1. archaic form of leggero

Inherited from Latin legere.

/ri.zulˈta.re/

Verb

  1. to turn out to be, prove to be or emerge as
  2. to appear or seem

Semi-learned borrowing from Latin resultāre, from resiliō.

/asˈsu.me.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to take on, assume
  2. (transitive) to employ, hire
  3. (transitive) to consume
    1. Synonym: consumare

Borrowed from Latin assūmere, from ad- + sūmō.

/konˈdur.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to lead, to guide, to escort
  2. (transitive) to drive (a car), to pilot (an aircraft), to steer (a boat)
  3. (transitive) to carry out, to conduct (an activity or initiative)
  4. (transitive) to lead, to experience (e.g. a happy life)
  5. (transitive, physics) to conduct
  6. (transitive, mathematics) to draw, to plot (a line)
  7. (intransitive) to lead (to a location; of a road) [auxiliary avere]
  8. (intransitive, sports) to be in the lead [auxiliary avere]

Inherited from Latin condūcere (“to lead, bring or draw together”), from con- +‎ dūcō (“lead”). By surface analysis, syncopic form of (archaic) conducere.

/di.mosˈtra.re/

Verb

  1. to show, to display, to manifest, to demonstrate, to look, to appear, to evince
    1. Synonyms: mostrare, manifestare, dare segno, spiegare
  2. to prove, to show, to establish, to demonstrate
    1. Synonyms: provare, stabilire

From Latin dēmōnstrāre.

/kaˈpi.re/

Verb

  1. (ambitransitive) to understand [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonyms: comprendere, intendere, afferrare
  2. (rare, intransitive, figurative) to fit, to be contained [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonyms: entrare, starci
    2. né mi potrà più capir nel pensiero ch’in animo celeste possa accendersi desiderio carnale
      nor will it be able to fit in my thoughts any more that carnal desire can be kindled in a heavenly soul
      (T. Tasso)

Inherited from Latin capiō (“to take in, understand”), from Proto-Italic *kapiō, from Proto-Indo-European *kh₂pyéti, from the root *kap- (“to seize, grab”). Compare Galician, Spanish, and Portuguese caber (“to fit”), Catalan capir (“to understand”), and German kapieren (“to understand”).

/ri.teˈne.re/

Verb

  1. (rare) to hold again
  2. to think, to believe, to consider
    1. Synonyms: considerare, credere, pensare
  3. to hold back, to restrain, to stop
    1. Synonyms: trattenere, fermare, arrestare
  4. (figurative) to retain (mentally), to remember, to keep in mind
  5. (figurative, literary) to repress (anger, a desire, a revolt, etc.)
  6. (finance) to retain, to withhold (a sum of money)
  7. (archaic) to keep (a secret)
  8. (archaic) to keep prisoner
  9. (archaic) to possess
  10. (archaic) to host

From Latin retinēre.

/proˈpor.re/

Verb

  1. to propose, suggest, or put forward
  2. to suggest (someone) (for a role, job position, etc.)
  3. (literary) to decide [with di (+ infinitive)]
  4. (literary) to destine
  5. (archaic) to start by saying

Usage Note

  1. (propose): when followed by another verb, must be followed either by di and an infinitive or che and the subjunctive form, as in mi hanno proposto di andare al cinema con loro or mi hanno proposto che io vada al cinema con loro ("they proposed [to me] that I go to the movie theater with them").

Derived from Latin prōpōnere (“to set forth; to propose; to declare”).

/resˈta.re/

Verb

  1. to stay, to remain (in a location)
  2. to be left, to remain, to be remaining
  3. to remain, to continue to be (with adjective complement)
  4. (literary) to stop
  5. (literary) to stop (doing something) [with di (+ infinitive) or da (+ infinitive)]

From Latin restāre, from re- + stō.

/de.riˈva.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to originate [with da ‘from’] (of a watercourse) [auxiliary essere]
  2. (intransitive, figurative) to derive [with da ‘from’] [auxiliary essere]
  3. (transitive) to divert (a watercourse)
  4. (transitive) to derive, to obtain (e.g. safety, security)
  5. (transitive, linguistics) to derive (a word, etc.)
  6. (transitive, mathematics) to differentiate (to calculate the derivative of a function)
  7. (intransitive, nautical) to drift (of a ship)
  8. (intransitive, aeronautics) to drift, to move sideways with respect to a predetermined course (of an airplane)

Borrowed from French dériver, from English drive or Dutch drijven (“to drag”).

/riˈkjɛ.de.re/

Verb

  1. to ask for, demand, apply for
    1. Synonyms: chiedere, domandare
  2. to request, exact, demand
    1. Synonyms: volere, esigere
  3. to require, need, take
    1. Synonyms: necessitare, volerci
  4. to ask again

From Vulgar Latin *requaerere, from Latin requīrere with dissimilation of /r–r/ to /d–r/, from re- with quaerere, from Proto-Indo-European.

/man.teˈne.re/

Verb

  1. to maintain, to keep
  2. to conserve
  3. to support (someone) financially or materially
  4. to govern
  5. to hold, to defend (a political possession, conquered territory, etc.)
  6. to uphold, to respect (a commitment, secret, etc.)
  7. (now southern Italy) to hold (something) in one's hand

From Late Latin manūtenēre (“to support”), from Latin manū (“with the hand”) + teneō (“to hold”). By surface analysis, mano +‎ tenere. Compare French maintenir, Spanish mantener, Portuguese manter.

/tras.feˈri.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to transfer, move, remove, shift
  2. (transitive, law) to convey, transfer

From Latin trānsferō.

/po.poˈla.re/

Adjective

  1. of the people, people's, popular
  2. folk, vernacular
  3. popular, pop, widespread, hot
    1. Synonyms: diffuso, conosciuto, famoso
  4. working-class
  5. low, cheap (plural; of prices)
    1. Synonyms: basso, economico

Verb

  1. to populate, to people
  2. to populate, to inhabit

From Latin populāris.

From popolo +‎ -are. Compare Catalan, Spanish, and Occitan poblar; French peupler; Portuguese povoar; Romanian popula.

/kosˈtrin.d͡ʒe.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to force, to compel, to constrain, to oblige (someone to do something)
    1. Synonyms: obbligare, forzare

Inherited from Latin cōnstringere.

/si.tuˈa.re/

Verb

  1. to situate, to place, to put, to locate, to set
    1. Synonyms: collocare, mettere, piazzare

Usage Note

  1. Usually in the passive.

Borrowed from Latin situāre.

/baˈza.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to base, ground, found
    1. Synonym: fondare

From base (“base; basis”) +‎ -are. Compare with Friulian basâ.

Verb

  1. (transitive) to choose
    1. Synonym: scerre

Inherited from Vulgar Latin *exēligere, from Latin ex (“out of, from”) + ēligere.

/ˈd͡ʒun.d͡ʒe.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to arrive, to reach, to come [auxiliary essere]
    1. Synonyms: arrivare, pervenire
  2. (transitive, literary) to join, to put together [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonyms: congiungere, unire

Inherited from Latin iungere (“to join”), from Proto-Italic *jungō, from Proto-Indo-European *yunégti ~ *yungénti, from the root *yewg-, whence also Romanian ajunge.

/di.kjaˈra.re/

Verb

  1. to declare, to announce, to proclaim, to state, to assert
  2. (card games) to bid

Synonym

  1. affermare
  2. annunciare
  3. asserire
  4. proclamare

From Latin dēclārāre.

/serˈvi.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive, also sports) to serve (in all senses)
  2. (intransitive) to serve [with a ‘someone’] [auxiliary avere]
  3. to be useful [auxiliary essere]
  4. to be necessary [with a ‘to someone’] [auxiliary essere]

From Latin servīre.

/ri.porˈta.re/

Verb

  1. to bring again, bring back, take back, carry back
    1. Synonym: restituire
  2. to report, carry, publish
    1. Synonym: ricordare
  3. to receive, get, carry off, suffer
    1. Synonyms: ricevere, ottenere, subire
  4. (mathematics) to carry

From Latin reportāre.

/ef.fet.tuˈa.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to effect, to carry out, to make
    1. Synonyms: fare, eseguire, condurre, realizzare

Borrowed from Medieval Latin effectuāre.

/ri.koˈnoʃ.ʃe.re/

Verb

  1. to recognize
  2. to acknowledge
  3. to admit
    1. Synonym: ammettere
  4. to identify
    1. Synonym: identificare
  5. to appreciate
    1. Synonym: apprezzare

From Latin recognōscere.

/riˈprɛn.de.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to take or grab again
    1. Synonyms: ripigliare, riafferrare, riacchiappare, prendere di nuovo
    2. to take (a means of transport) again
    3. to take (a road, street, etc.) again
    4. to catch again
  2. (transitive) to catch up to
  3. (transitive) to take back
    1. Synonyms: prendere indietro, riavere
    2. to regain (confidence, courage, etc.)
    3. to tack back into one's control; to reconquer
  4. (ambitransitive) to resume, go back to, go on, continue [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonyms: ricominciare, continuare, rifare, riattaccare, soggiungere
  5. (transitive) to take, shoot, film, portray, set (of a picture, movie, etc.)
    1. Synonyms: ritrarre, inquadrare, filmare, fotografare
  6. (transitive) to scold, reprimand, berate
    1. Synonyms: ammonire, correggere, criticare, biasimare, sgridare, rimproverare
  7. (transitive) to take hold of, seize, or strike (someone) again (of a sensation, feeling, etc.)
    1. Synonyms: tornare a colpire, assalire di nuovo, sorprendere
  8. (transitive) to emulate
  9. (transitive) to touch up or tighten (a seam, garment, etc.)
    1. Synonyms: ridurre, rimpicciolire, restringere, stringere
  10. (transitive) to repeat (a motif, design element, etc.)
    1. Synonym: richiamare
  11. (intransitive) to revive [auxiliary essere] (of a plant)

From Latin reprehendere.

Verb

  1. (transitive) to climb again, to ascend again
    1. Synonym: rimontare
  2. (intransitive) to climb again, to go up again [auxiliary essere]
  3. (intransitive) to mentally return to past events; to remember [with a] [auxiliary essere]
    1. Synonym: riportarsi
  4. (intransitive) to come to or figure out the beginning or origin [with a] [auxiliary essere]
  5. (intransitive) to date back [with a ‘to’] [auxiliary essere]
  6. (intransitive) to regain (a lost position or condition) [with in] [auxiliary essere]
  7. (intransitive) to rise or increase again [auxiliary essere]
    1. Synonyms: rincarare, aumentare, rialzarsi

From Vulgar Latin *resalīre. Synchronically derivable from ri- +‎ salire.

/sos.ti.tuˈi.re/

Verb

  1. to substitute (someone/something) [with a ‘for someone/something else’]
  2. to replace (someone/something) [with con ‘with someone/something else’]
    1. Synonyms: cambiare, rimpiazzare
  3. to replace, to take the place of, to stand in for (someone/something) (temporarily or permanently)

From Latin substituō.

/adˈd͡ʒun.d͡ʒe.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to add, to append

From Latin adiungere (“add, join to”).

/af.ferˈma.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to declare, to affirm, to state, to claim, to assert
    1. Synonyms: dichiarare, sostenere, asserire

From Latin affirmāre.

/no.miˈna.re/

Verb

  1. to name, call, dub
  2. to mention
  3. to nominate, designate, elect, appoint
  4. to institute
  5. to constitute

From Latin nōmināre, from nōmen (“name”).

/kon.senˈti.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to agree, to assent, to consent [auxiliary avere]
    1. Synonym: acconsentire
  2. (transitive) to allow, to let, to give, to enable
    1. Synonyms: permettere, concedere, lasciare
  3. (transitive, literary) to admit (e.g. the truth)
    1. Synonym: ammettere
  4. (transitive, uncommon) to share (a feeling)

Borrowed from Latin cōnsentīre.

/ka.rat.te.ridˈd͡za.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to characterize
  2. (transitive) to be characteristic of

From carattere +‎ -izzare.

/in.konˈtra.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to meet, come across, bump into, run into, find, encounter
    1. Synonyms: imbattersi, trovare
  2. (transitive, sports) to play, fight
  3. (intransitive, rare) to happen

Derived from Late Latin incontrā. By surface analysis, incontro +‎ -are. Compare Portuguese and Spanish encontrar, French rencontrer.

/ab.ban.doˈna.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to abandon (to leave behind)
  2. (by extension, transitive) to give up on, to abandon
    1. Synonyms: rinunciare a, ritirarsi da
  3. (by extension, intransitive) to give up
    1. Synonyms: arrendersi, dare forfait, desistere, lasciare perdere, (colloquial) mollare, rinunciare, ritirarsi
  4. (by extension, transitive) to neglect
    1. Synonym: trascurare
  5. (transitive) to loosen
    1. Synonym: allentare
  6. (transitive) to relax
    1. Synonym: rilassare

Borrowed from Old French abandoner.

/in.ter.preˈta.re/

Verb

  1. to interpret (all senses)
  2. to perform

From Latin interpretārī.

/in.seˈri.re/

Verb

  1. to insert
  2. to enclose
  3. to embed

From Latin īnserere.

/salˈva.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to save, rescue, retrieve, deliver
    1. Synonym: mettere in salvo
  2. (transitive) to save, guard, safeguard, protect, defend
    1. Synonyms: proteggere, salvaguardare, difendere

From Late Latin salvāre (“to save”), from Latin salvus. Compare French sauver, Portuguese and Spanish salvar.

/ap.par.teˈne.re/

Verb

  1. (intransitive) to belong [with a ‘to’] [auxiliary essere or avere]
  2. (intransitive) to concern, to pertain to [with a] [auxiliary essere or avere]

From Late Latin appertinēre, from Latin pertinēre; influenced by pars (“part”). Compare English appertain.

/spoˈza.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to cause (someone) to get married, to give a spouse to, to marry (someone to someone else)
  2. (transitive, figurative) to embrace, to espouse, to join

From Latin spōnsāre.

/kolˈpi.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to hit, strike, smite
  2. (transitive) to affect
  3. (transitive) to surprise, impress

From colpo +‎ -ire.

/or.ɡa.nidˈd͡za.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to organize, arrange, set up

Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin organizāre (“to organize”).

/forˈni.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to supply, to provide, to furnish, to give, to yield
    1. Synonyms: dare, provvedere
  2. (transitive) to equip
    1. Synonyms: attrezzare, equipaggiare

Borrowed from Old French fornir, of Germanic origin, from Frankish *frumjan (“to complete, execute”), from Proto-Germanic *frumjaną (“to further, promote”), from Proto-Indo-European *promo- (“front, forward”). Compare French fournir, Catalan fornir, Spanish and Portuguese fornecer, English furnish.

/rakˈkɔʎ.ʎe.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to pick up, glean
  2. (transitive) to pick, pluck, harvest, reap
  3. (transitive) to bring together, assemble

From Latin recolligere. Compare Sicilian ricògghiri.

/tras.forˈma.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to change, transform, convert, turn
    1. Synonyms: cambiare, convertire, tramutare

From Latin trānsfōrmāre.

/desˈkri.ve.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to describe (in all senses)

From Latin dēscrībere (“to describe”).

/ri.veˈla.re/

Verb

  1. (transitive) to reveal, disclose, let out, make known, tell
    1. Synonyms: svelare, palesare, rendere
  2. (transitive) to reveal, show, display
    1. Synonym: manifestare
  3. (transitive) to detect
    1. Synonym: rilevare
  4. (transitive) to veil again; to hide or conceal again
  5. (transitive) to furnish again with sails

Borrowed from Latin revēlāre.

From ri- +‎ velare (“to veil”).

From ri- +‎ velare (“to furnish with sails”).

/tenˈta.re/

Verb

  1. to try, to attempt
    1. Synonym: provare
  2. to tempt, to lure, to attract, to entice
    1. Synonym: indurre in tentazione
  3. (literary) to touch lightly

From Latin temptāre.
